_comment: What each fixture's ACC-RESULT.md is supposed to say, and why.
These expectations describe the CURRENT routing block. They are not a
transcript of what any particular runtime said - see results/ for that.
A recorded result that predates a block change can legitimately fail an
expectation here; check_results.py reports that as a mismatch with the
recorded date, not as a defect in the runtime.
'routed_to_any_of' is a set because several commands are correct answers
to 'review the finished work' when gstack and Advanced Planning are both
installed, and the round was never trying to pin which one.
The empty list [] means the only correct answer is NONE: there is no
command to run and the runtime must say so rather than name one to be
'known_divergences' lists cells where a recorded result no longer matches
because the BLOCK changed, not because the runtime was wrong. They are
reported as DIVERGED and do not fail the run, so a genuine regression
still turns the check red. Each carries the reason and what would close
it. Deleting an entry without re-running the round is how a checker stops

all-installed.why: The positive control, and the only fixture where gstack (true) and gstack-to-plans (false) diverge. A fix that made every answer NONE would pass both negative fixtures and be worthless; this one catches that. The gstack/gstack-to-plans split proves a runtime reads per-component rather than per-vendor.

2.why: SP-1: with Advanced Planning installed the spec goes to .advanced-plans/specs/, not the skill's own default. SP-2: the terminal step is phase planning, not writing-plans.

3.why: Front-door rule 6 or 7. Both gstack and Advanced Planning are installed, so more than one route is defensible.

only-superpowers.why: The decoy. A .advanced-plans/specs/borrowed.md directory is present but Advanced Planning is NOT installed. The block says a directory is data, not an installation.

1.why: gstack is not installed, so there is no /office-hours to invoke. Naming one is the failure the manifest gate exists to prevent.

2.terminal_step_note: Advanced Planning is absent, so the block's fallback is writing-plans - but only when that skill is actually present, and this fixture plants only brainstorming. The correct answer is therefore conversation, and naming writing-plans is naming a skill that could not be loaded. This expectation post-dates c83c90e; before it the block was silent here and four of five runtimes named writing-plans. See the evidence file.
2.why: SP-1 in the other direction: the spec goes to the skill's own upstream default, and no .advanced-plans/ path is invented despite the decoy sitting right there.

3.why: Neither gstack nor Advanced Planning is installed, so no review command exists.

broken-manifest.why: The discriminator. Every sentinel is genuinely on disk and global gstack is visible in the fake HOME, but .aaw/installed.json is truncated and unparseable. A reader that probes the filesystem instead of the manifest gets all three wrong. NOTE: NONE x3 is also what a runtime that never read the block produces, which is why this fixture is never run alone.

1.why: Malformed manifest means treat every component as not installed.

2.why: Same. Including brainstorming, whose sentinel is on disk. The design itself is still expected to be written - the envelope asks for the work, not just the report - but not under a .advanced-plans/ path this project has given no evidence exists.

known_divergences.reason: Recorded before c83c90e, when the block was silent on a skill that is manifest-installed but not present on disk. These four named writing-plans by following the block; codex checked and declined. codex was right and the block was wrong, which is what c83c90e fixed. Re-running only-superpowers against the current block is what closes this - until then it is recorded, not hidden.
